clue.text: Jointly endorse function for broadcasters

indicators.note: what is said on air is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: cosine is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A request that two radio or TV stations put their names together on some job.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosign is to add one's signature alongside another's, giving joint approval to a document.

clue.text: Woman seizing diamonds in barrel; she'll pay for it here?

indicators.note: the woman holding diamonds goes inside the barrel

parts.note: a cask is a barrel

indicators.note: the woman takes hold of the diamonds, which go inside her

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman hiding stolen jewels in a barrel will be made to pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She'll pay for it' sounds like punishment; it is a shopper paying at a till.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash desk is the counter in a shop where customers pay for their purchases.

clue.text: Sneering sort's second secret spot

parts.note: a quiet corner is a secluded place

explanation.surface: A disdainful person's second hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorner is someone who shows contempt or derision for others.

clue.text: At first, groom falling short of embracing humourless wife — it could produce fireworks

indicators.note: At first takes just the opening letter of groom

parts.note: the first letter of groom is taken

indicators.note: the word for falling short of wraps around the next letters

parts.note: under means below or short of a target, as in under budget
po, short for po-faced, means humourless and disapproving

explanation.surface: A wedding scene: a groom who is no match for his humourless wife, with sparks to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fireworks' suggests a marital row; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder is the explosive mixture packed into fireworks to make them burst.

clue.text: Simplest form of life in zoo or apt compound

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients together, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A biology aside about the most primitive creatures turning up in a zoo or some suitable mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Protozoa are single-celled organisms, among the most basic kinds of living thing.

clue.text: Incorrectly depreciate solo instrument getting stellar reception

indicators.note: incorrectly means put in the wrong order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soloist's instrument wrongly devalued but then given a starry welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stellar reception' looks like rave reviews; it is literal reception of signals from stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio telescope is an astronomical instrument that picks up radio waves from stars and galaxies.

clue.text: Mountainous region tense I predict

parts.note: taken as written
to bet that something will happen is to predict it

explanation.surface: A nervous person forecasting something about a mountain area.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a high Himalayan plateau region, often called the roof of the world.

clue.text: Huge number sick in heaven

indicators.note: the word for sick is placed inside the word for heaven

parts.note: Zion is used for the heavenly city or paradise
ill means sick or unwell

explanation.surface: A great many people falling ill in paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: A zillion is an informal word for an enormous, unspecified number.

clue.text: Answer Tories, perhaps justifiably

parts.note: the political right includes Conservatives, or Tories, as an example

explanation.surface: A defence of the Conservatives' reply as reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Aright is an old adverb meaning correctly or properly, close to justifiably.

clue.text: Erratic teen's test drive is personal concern

indicators.note: erratic means unpredictable and irregular, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A wayward teenager's driving test is a matter of private worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A vested interest is a personal stake in an outcome, usually for one's own benefit.

clue.text: Overindulge hoax involving new river running west

indicators.note: the hoax word takes in, or involves, the next letter

parts.note: a spoof is a hoax or send-up

indicators.note: in an across clue, running west means reading right to left

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone spoiled by a trick involving a westward-flowing river.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoonfeed is to pamper by doing everything for someone, an indulgence carried too far.

clue.text: Estonian, Latvian or Lithuanian island dish

parts.note: a Balt is a native of any of the three Baltic states

explanation.surface: A quiz-style question about a dish from an island in the Baltic region.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spiced curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, associated with Birmingham.

clue.text: Ned and I possibly get tuck externally

indicators.note: possibly signals that Ned and I might be shuffled into another arrangement

parts.note: out means outside, away from home

explanation.surface: Two people, Ned and the speaker, wondering about grabbing a bite somewhere away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British schoolboy slang for food. The clue also reads in reverse: DINE with 'out' as an anagram signal yields NED I.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine out is to eat a meal at a restaurant rather than at home; tuck is slang for food.

clue.text: One shutting eyes to reality in east of Germany elaborately decorated

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
rich décor is lavish and ornate

explanation.surface: Someone living in denial in an ornately furnished house in eastern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Ostrich is figurative here, from the myth that the bird buries its head in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrich, figuratively, is a person who refuses to face unpleasant facts.

clue.text: Ogre removing king died in scrap

indicators.note: the king's letter is taken away from the ogre's name
the letter for died is put in where the king was

parts.note: Shrek is the ogre of the animated films

explanation.surface: A monster loses a monarch, who dies in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight but is the definition in its sense of a small fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny strip or fragment, just as a scrap is a small leftover piece.

clue.text: Sound to acquire comfortable house

indicators.note: the ringing sound gets hold of the next word, which goes inside it

parts.note: ding is the sound of a bell
well off, or simply well, means comfortably placed

explanation.surface: Financially sound enough to buy a cosy home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective for being solvent; it is the noise of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a place where people live, the same as a house used as a noun.

clue.text: Unwilling to shelter adult a little is detestable

indicators.note: the word for unwilling gives shelter to the next letter, which goes inside

parts.note: loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: Refusing to give a grown-up even a bit of shelter is hateful.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome describes something that causes hatred or disgust, the same as detestable.

clue.text: Subs' bench?

parts.note: on the surface the substitutes' seat at a match; really the newspaper subeditors' work table

explanation.walkthrough: The image is of football reserves on the sidelines; subs are also newspaper subeditors, who work at the desk where news is handled.
explanation.definitionFit: The news desk is the department and workstation of a newspaper where stories are edited.

clue.text: End of marriage, odd divorce

indicators.note: End of picks out the final letter of the word marriage

parts.note: the final letter of marriage is taken
strange means odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A marriage ends in a peculiar divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate or separate people, as a divorce separates a couple; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Possible means of providing unloved oiks access to the slopes

definitions.text: Possible means of providing unloved oiks access to the slopes

parts.words: Possible means of providing unloved oiks access to the slopes
parts.note: on the surface, a way of getting louts nobody likes up the mountain; read as wordplay, oiks without love (the zero-shaped letter) raised upward by the answer's second word

explanation.surface: A thought about how louts nobody likes might be taken up to the ski runs.
explanation.walkthrough: This works in reverse: the answer read as an instruction, with lift meaning raise it up in a down light, turns its first word into the oiks minus love. An oik is British slang for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift is a cable-drawn system carrying skiers up the mountainside to the runs.

clue.text: A pay increase — result!

parts.note: taken as written
a rise is a British term for a raise in salary

explanation.surface: Someone celebrating getting a raise at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Result!' reads as a cheer; it is the verb meaning to follow as a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to come about as a consequence, which is what to result means.

clue.text: One upset solid base put on a pedestal

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Someone toppling a solid base that something stood on.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise is to admire excessively, which is what putting someone on a pedestal means.

clue.text: Fruit purée and game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gourd such as butternut, botanically a fruit
second meaning: to crush or pulp something
third meaning: the racket sport played in a walled court

explanation.surface: A menu note about blended fruit with game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word, read as a single menu item.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a gourd-like vegetable fruit, the act of crushing to pulp, and a racket sport.

clue.text: Grass that is providing fast drink

parts.note: quick is another name for couch grass, also called quitch
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Some grass, it seems, makes for a speedy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickie is a hurried drink taken in a spare moment, especially at a pub.

clue.text: Sven or Kasper holds up Norwegian cash

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom
the names hold the letters within their run

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Sven, the word or and the start of Kasper

explanation.surface: Two Scandinavian men holding up a bank for its money.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency unit of Norway, so it is Norwegian money.

clue.text: Charlie, with hint of anger, ridicules collusion

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: hint of takes just the opening letter of anger

parts.note: just the opening letter of anger is taken
to hoot at someone is to jeer at them

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie mocking others with a touch of anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is to be in secret partnership, a conspiratorial collusion.

clue.text: French pal has energy for Spanish counterpart

parts.note: ami is the French word for friend
go means vigour or energy

explanation.surface: A French friend swaps energy for a Spanish equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, matching the French ami.

clue.text: Arranged live expos for Shell?

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a different order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An oil company putting on live exhibitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' suggests the oil company; it is an artillery shell, which the question mark marks as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is an explosive projectile, so it is one example of an explosive.

clue.text: Article runs in sock, last to go previously

indicators.note: the article and runs are put inside the word for sock

parts.note: to sock someone is to hit them hard
the is the definite article
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of go

parts.note: only the final letter of go is taken

explanation.surface: A sock that loses an item in the wash, with the last of it going.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means up to now, or until this time, which is what previously means.

clue.text: Adorn bottom of lake with impudence first off

parts.note: a lake bed is the bottom of a lake

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Decorating the lake floor, with cheek coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedeck is to decorate lavishly, a synonym of adorn.
